title: PoLARIS: a self-driving microfluidic lab finds brighter lead-free perovskite nanoplatelets
summary: A closed-loop microfluidic platform ran 120 experiments in one 12-hour campaign on double perovskite nanoplatelets with up to six elements and identified the brightest lead-free composition found in that campaign. The press release gives no numerical photoluminescence gain, so the improvement is not quantified in the sources checked. Validation is the authors' own experimental measurements, and the paper should be checked for the brightness figures.
ai_technology: PoLARIS (microfluidic self-driving lab with closed-loop experiment selection)
organization: North Carolina State University; Brown University

evidence.tested: Lab experiments in one 12-hour campaign of 120 runs identified the brightest lead-free composition found in that campaign; the abstract does not report photoluminescence measurements.
evidence.unknown: The press release gives no numerical brightness gain; the abstract does not state limitations.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning guided closed-loop experiment selection on a modular microfluidic reactor.
